spec.note:
FIRST ACTION, EXACT: before any other line of code, run
  print("APIBEGIN", sorted([n for n in dir() if not n.startswith("_")]))
  print("APIEND")
so the console shows the complete list of names your program runs with.
Confirmed primitives you may use: navigate_to(name); get_observation() -> obs with obs["robot0_robotview"]["images"]["rgb"] (uint8 HxWx3), ["images"]["depth"] (float metres, ~0 = invalid), ["intrinsics"] (3x3), ["pose_mat"] (4x4 camera->world); segment_sam3_text_prompt(rgb, text) -> list of dicts {"mask": bool HxW, "score": float} (empty list if not found); segment_sam3_point_prompt(rgb, (u, v)) -> same; point_prompt_molmo(rgb, text) -> {text: (u, v) or (None, None)}; plan_grasp(depth, intrinsics, segmap_int_HxW) -> (poses (N,4,4) in the CAMERA frame, scores (N,)); solve_ik(pos_world_xyz, quat_wxyz) -> 7 joints; move_to_joints(joints); open_gripper(); close_gripper().
Do NOT guess or assume any other control function exists (no turn_knob / press_button / actuate / open_door / close_drawer etc. unless the APIBEGIN list shows such a name AND a trial call with try/except succeeds). If the appliance part you must actuate (knob, button, lever, lid, door, drawer, slider) has no convenience function in the list, manipulate it physically: grasp it and sweep the gripper along the motion, or press with the closed gripper.
Robustness: pixel is (u, v); use depth[v, u]; pose_mat @ [x, y, d, 1.0]; wrap every IK/move in try/except; never raise; a printed "success" is not the success check - the simulator checks the final state, and it usually requires the gripper to be 0.15-0.25 m away from the objects at the end (finish with the gripper up 0.12 and back 0.10 after every release).
